question: Implementing regulation (EU) 2026/888 of 20 April 2026 lays down the management modes for tariff rate quotas on products originating in Mercosur countries. This arrangement marks a significant change by allowing partner countries to notify the allocation of volumes amongst their operators and, in effect, to intervene in the allocation of quotas.

The mechanism is a departure from the principle of tariff quotas being managed entirely by the EU via its export licence system. By making access to quotas contingent on approval from export authorities, it poses a real risk of a partial transfer of control to third countries or private companies.

This development raises serious concerns about adherence to the principles of open, transparent and non‑discriminatory access to quotas. It could lead to volumes being concentrated in the hands of a limited number of dominant stakeholders, particularly the Brazilian group JBS, putting EU operators and vulnerable agricultural sectors at a disadvantage.
It also sets a precedent that could weaken the EU’s commercial sovereignty in the long term. In view of this: 1.
What action does the Commission intend to take to avoid quotas being monopolised by a limited number of dominant operators in Mercosur countries?
Does it plan to introduce a revision clause for this instrument?
Supporter1
This question is supported by a Member other than the authors: Csaba Dömötör (PfE).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.7.2026) Import Tariff Rate Quotas (TRQs) established under the EU-Mercosur Interim Trade Agreement (ITA) are administered exclusively by the EU, as laid down in Regulation (EU) 2026/9961. This Regulation introduced in Implementing Regulations (EU) 2020/7612 and (EU) 2020/19883 rules for the management of those import TRQs for agricultural products.

In accordance with Article 3.30 of the ITA, ‘products exported under tariff rate quotas granted by the EU shall be accompanied by an official document issued by the Signatory Mercosur States’. Such a document is understood to allow Mercosur Signatory States to verify quota allocation among themselves. The model of this document was published in the Official Journal on 14 April 20264.

The Commission will closely monitor imports under TRQs. The agreement also provides for consultation and dispute settlement mechanisms. The Commission, in line with Regulation (EU) 2026/6875 will monitor import flows and price trends and will report regularly to the European Parliament and the Council.
